title: Vertex Modules, Rationality, and Logarithmic Regimes

items.title: Formal delta substitution identity for module Jacobi
items.statement: Prove the formal delta substitution identity that identifies the difference of the two module Jacobi delta expansions with z_2^(-1) delta((z_1-z_0)/z_2), using the declared binomial expansion conventions.

items.title: Module for an ordinary vertex algebra
items.statement: Define a left module over an ordinary, non-super complex vertex algebra by a lower-truncated field map, vacuum action, and the formal module Jacobi identity, with the formal-delta expansion conventions stated explicitly.

items.title: Conformal vertex algebra of CFT type
items.statement: Define a CFT-type vertex operator algebra with conformal vector, mode convention Y(omega,z)=sum L_n z^(-n-2), Virasoro central charge, translation L_-1=T, nonnegative integer grading, finite-dimensional graded pieces, and V_0=C1.

items.title: Admissible module for a vertex operator algebra
items.statement: Define an admissible module as a nonnegatively integer-graded module for a nonnegatively graded VOA, with the exact conformal-weight mode shift and no assumption that L_0 is semisimple.

items.title: Grading-restricted generalized module
items.statement: Define generalized L_0-eigenspaces, finite-dimensional generalized weight spaces, and a lower-bounded weight condition for modules over a conformal vertex algebra.

items.title: Ordinary module
items.statement: Define an ordinary module as a grading-restricted generalized module on which L_0 acts semisimply; state the eigenspace and lower-bound conditions separately from admissibility.

items.title: Positive-energy module
items.statement: Fix positive energy by requiring a nonzero ordinary module with spectrum in one lowest-weight translate h+Z_{≥0} and a nonzero lowest eigenspace; distinguish this extra spectrum condition from the bare module axioms.

items.title: Rationality in the admissible-module convention
items.statement: Define rationality by complete reducibility of every admissible module, declare that finite number of irreducibles and C_2-cofiniteness are separate properties, and state that other conventions may package additional hypotheses.

items.title: C2-cofiniteness
items.statement: Define C_2(V)=span{u_(-2)v : u,v in V} and C_2-cofiniteness by finite dimension of V/C_2(V), without asserting rationality or modularity consequences.

items.title: Logarithmic generalized module
items.statement: Define a logarithmic module to be a grading-restricted generalized module on which L_0 is not semisimple, equivalently with a nontrivial finite Jordan chain in some generalized weight space.

items.title: Rank-one Heisenberg oscillator fields and vacuum space
items.statement:
Let $P=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]$ be the polynomial algebra whose elements involve finitely many indeterminates, as in [[def-polynomial-ring-on-a-family-of-indeterminates]]. Give $x_r$ degree $r$ and write $P_d$ for its degree-$d$ subspace. On $P$, put

$$a_{-r}=x_r\cdot,\qquad a_r=r\frac{\partial}{\partial x_r}\quad(r\ge1),\qquad a_0=0,\qquad \mathbf1=1,\qquad T=\sum_{r\ge1}r x_{r+1}\frac{\partial}{\partial x_r}.$$

Every sum of operators here is applied to a polynomial and is then finite. Define $a(z)=\sum_{n\in\mathbb Z}a_nz^{-n-1}$, in the conventions of [[def-formal-distribution-on-a-vector-space]], and the divided derivative $b_r(z)=\partial_z^{r-1}a(z)/(r-1)!$ for $r\ge1$. In normal ordering, all modes $a_n$ with $n<0$ are moved to the left of all modes with $n\ge0$, preserving their respective internal orders. For a polynomial monomial $v=x_{r_1}\cdots x_{r_s}$ define the candidate field

$$Y(v,z)={:}b_{r_1}(z)\cdots b_{r_s}(z){:},\qquad Y(1,z)=I.$$

The empty normal product is the identity. The same-sign modes commute, so the formula is symmetric in the listed factors; it is extended linearly from the polynomial monomial basis. Set $\omega=\tfrac12 x_1^2$. The well-defined state-field and conformal-VOA structure on this vacuum space are proved in [[thm-rank-one-heisenberg-vertex-operator-algebra]]. The symbol $a_n$ is a current mode; in particular $Y(x_1,z)=a(z)$ and $Y(\omega,z)=\sum_nL(n)z^{-n-2}$ use different mode shifts.
items.axiom_use: None; explicit polynomial monomial bases, finite matching sums and degreewise formal calculations.

sources.title: Tomoyuki Arakawa and Anne Moreau, Arc Spaces and Vertex Algebras
Christophe Nozaradan, Introduction to Vertex Algebras

items.title: The rank-one Heisenberg vacuum space is a conformal VOA of central charge one
items.statement:
The data in [[def-rank-one-heisenberg-vertex-algebra]] define a vertex algebra with the displayed normal-monomial state fields. With $\omega=\tfrac12x_1^2$ it is a conformal vertex algebra of CFT type in the convention of [[def-conformal-vertex-algebra]], with central charge $1$. Its conformal modes are

$$L(n)=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}{:}a_k a_{n-k}{:},\qquad L(0)=\sum_{r\ge1}r x_r\frac{\partial}{\partial x_r},\qquad L(-1)=T.$$

Each quadratic-mode sum is finite on every vector. The weight-$d$ space is $P_d$, with the finite basis of monomials $\prod_r x_r^{m_r}$ satisfying $\sum_r r m_r=d$; in particular $P_0=\mathbb C\mathbf1$.
items.axiom_use: None; explicit polynomial monomial bases, finite matching sums and degreewise formal calculations.

sources.title: Tomoyuki Arakawa and Anne Moreau, Arc Spaces and Vertex Algebras
Christophe Nozaradan, Introduction to Vertex Algebras

items.title: Heisenberg normal-ordered fields give modules with an arbitrary zero-mode action
items.statement:
Let $V=P$ be the rank-one Heisenberg vertex algebra of [[thm-rank-one-heisenberg-vertex-operator-algebra]]. For any complex vector space $E$ and any $A\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(E)$, set $F(E,A)=P\otimes E$ and define

$$a_{-r}=x_r\cdot\otimes I_E,\qquad a_r=r\partial_{x_r}\otimes I_E\ (r\ge1),\qquad a_0=I_P\otimes A.$$

Write $a^F(z)=\sum_na_nz^{-n-1}$ and $b_r^F(z)=\partial_z^{r-1}a^F(z)/(r-1)!$. With the same negative/nonnegative-mode normal ordering as [[def-rank-one-heisenberg-vertex-algebra]], put

$$Y_F(x_{r_1}\cdots x_{r_s},z)={:}b_{r_1}^F(z)\cdots b_{r_s}^F(z){:},\qquad Y_F(1,z)=I.$$

These fields give a $V$-module in the full formal-Jacobi convention of [[def-vertex-algebra-module]]. In particular, no diagonalizability or nilpotence condition on $A$ is required. For $v\in P_w$ and $f\in P_d\otimes E$, each mode satisfies

$$v^F_{(k)}f\in P_{d+w-k-1}\otimes E,$$

where negative degrees are zero. Thus the fields are lower truncated, and this is an admissible nonnegative integer grading whenever the module is viewed over the conformal VOA. No logarithmic powers occur in $Y_F$ itself.
items.axiom_use: None; explicit polynomial monomial bases, finite matching sums and degreewise formal calculations.

sources.title: Tomoyuki Arakawa and Anne Moreau, Arc Spaces and Vertex Algebras
Christophe Nozaradan, Introduction to Vertex Algebras

items.title: A rank-one Heisenberg Jordan Fock module is grading-restricted and logarithmic
items.statement:
Let $E=\mathbb C e_0\oplus\mathbb C e_1$, define $Ne_0=0$, $Ne_1=e_0$, and let $A_\lambda=\lambda I+N$ for $\lambda\in\mathbb C$. The oscillator module $F_\lambda=F(E,A_\lambda)$ constructed in [[lem-heisenberg-normal-ordered-fields-satisfy-module-jacobi]] is a module over the conformal CFT-type rank-one Heisenberg VOA of central charge $1$. Its conformal modes are

$$L_F(n)=\frac12\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}{:}a_k a_{n-k}{:},\qquad L_F(0)=D\otimes I_E+\tfrac12 I_P\otimes A_\lambda^2=D\otimes I_E+\tfrac{\lambda^2}{2}I+\lambda I_P\otimes N,$$

where $D|_{P_d}=dI$. The degree spaces $P_d\otimes E$ give an admissible grading and are exactly the generalized weight spaces of weights $d+\lambda^2/2$, of dimension $2\dim P_d$. Thus $F_\lambda$ is grading-restricted generalized. It is logarithmic exactly when $\lambda\ne0$; at $\lambda=0$ it is ordinary despite its nonsemisimple current zero mode. In particular $F_1$ has $a_0=I+N$ and $L_F(0)|_E=\tfrac12I+N$.
items.axiom_use: None; explicit polynomial monomial bases, finite matching sums and degreewise formal calculations.

title: Vertex Modules, Rationality, and Logarithmic Regimes: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The one-dimensional vertex operator algebra is rational
items.statement: Verify that the specified one-dimensional structure is a conformal vertex algebra of CFT type, then prove every admissible module is a direct sum of one-dimensional simple modules, recording the use of choice for arbitrary bases.

items.title: Finite simple labels alone do not imply a semisimple module category
items.statement: For the dual-number commutative vertex algebra with T=0, show that its finite-dimensional constant-field module subcategory has one simple isomorphism class but its regular module is a nonsplit self-extension; state that this is not a counterexample to a rationality theorem for conformal VOAs because no conformal vector is supplied.

items.title: An explicit logarithmic conformal Heisenberg module
items.statement:
For the rank-one Heisenberg conformal VOA, take $F_1=\mathbb C[x_1,x_2,\ldots]\otimes E$ with $E=\mathbb C e_0\oplus\mathbb C e_1$, $Ne_1=e_0$, $Ne_0=0$, and $a_0=I+N$. The positive modes are $a_r=r\partial_{x_r}$ and negative modes are $a_{-r}=x_r$. Its fields are the normal-ordered divided derivatives in the A-page construction, not constant dual-number fields. It is an admissible, grading-restricted logarithmic module, and on its lowest generalized weight space

$$a_0|_E=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad L_F(0)|_E=\begin{pmatrix}\tfrac12&1\\0&\tfrac12\end{pmatrix}.$$
items.axiom_use: None; explicit polynomial monomial bases, finite matching sums and degreewise formal calculations.
